name: Los Angeles high-water residual (October 2026)
as_of: 24 Oct 2026 (NOAA CO-OPS Los Angeles observations through 16 Oct checked)
headline: Preliminary NOAA CO-OPS observations at Los Angeles were above hourly tide predictions during 13–16 October 2026. The residual does not identify its cause; the claimed Kelvin-wave and marine-heatwave contributions are unverified.
numbers: +0.525 to +1.444 ft (13–16 Oct; hourly-mean residual range)
timeline: At NOAA CO-OPS Los Angeles station 9410660, daily means of hourly observed-minus-predicted water levels were +0.946 to +1.082 ft; individual hourly-mean residuals across the four days ranged from +0.525 to +1.444 ft. The 6-minute observed water-level API records were preliminary when checked.
No event-specific sea-level decomposition was found to quantify contributions from an equatorial Kelvin wave, local marine heatwave, long-term sea-level rise, tides, storm surge, or swell.

sections.The observation: NOAA CO-OPS provides preliminary six-minute water-level observations and harmonic tide predictions for station 9410660. For 13–16 October, hourly means of the observed series minus predictions at matching UTC hours were positive; the daily means ranged from +0.946 to +1.082 ft. This is a station-level residual, not an attribution to a particular ocean or atmospheric process.
sections.What is not established: No primary source or reproducible calculation was found for a 9–12 inch Kelvin-wave contribution, a 6–10 inch marine-heatwave contribution, or the additional long-term-rise and tidal-datum amounts claimed in the prior text. The residual can include multiple processes and cannot be partitioned from this station comparison alone.
sections.Interpretation: Equatorial Kelvin waves and coastal-trapped waves are recognized ocean dynamics, but the available ERA5 diagnostic measures equatorial zonal-wind anomalies and burst counts; it does not measure coastal sea level or quantify a wave contribution at Los Angeles.
